newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN MUST BOUNCE BACK TO KEEP TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN MUST BOUNCE BACK TO KEEP TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Bayern Munich face a test of character as they try to show in two awkward games this week that they have put Sunday's 5-2 drubbing at Bayer Leverkusen behind them and can keep their German title bid on track.
Striker Juergen Klinsmann said several weeks ago that this week would show what Bayern were made of -- but the collapse of their defence against Leverkusen was not the start they had hoped for.

Bayern's first defeat in 13 matches allowed reigning champions Borussia Dortmund to take over at the top of the Bundesliga on goal difference. Ominously for both sides, VfB Stuttgart returned to their free-scoring early-season form with an imperious 4-1 win over troubled Hamburg.
On Wednesday Bayern travel to promoted Arminia Bielefeld, who have won four of their last five home games but are unlikely to punish the erratic Munich defence as Leverkusen did.
And on Saturday they entertain in-form Schalke, who have not lost nor conceded a goal in eight league matches and beat Bayern's UEFA Cup conquerors Valencia 2-0 in midweek.

Coach Giovanni Trapattoni accused his expensive professionals of going into Saturday's top-of-the-table clash as though it were a friendly but said the defeat could be "a valuable lesson for us if we still want to be champions".

In Tuesday's main match, Stuttgart travel to Cologne with their title hopes revived but still not sure whether trainer Joachim Loew, given a one-year contract after taking over as caretaker at the start of the season, will be kept on.
"If we win in Cologne then anything may be possible," said Stuttgart striker Fredi Bobic, scorer of 13 league goals this season.
At the other end of the table, Hamburg slithered further into crisis on Monday.

As club chairman Uwe Seeler struggled with a conflict over the board's business practices, the club said midfielder Markus Schupp had received a formal written caution after criticising coach Felix Magath's tough training methods in interviews.

Magath dropped Schupp from Tuesday's important bottom-half clash against a resurgent Borussia Moenchengladbach -- unbeaten in four games under new trainer Hannes Bongartz -- and made clear he was unlikely to play him again.
"Schupp has done a lot of damage to the team," Magath said.
Dortmund have perhaps the easiest task in a full midweek programme with a home match on Wednesday against Hansa Rostock, lying one from bottom.
Leverkusen will try to build on their towering performance against Bayern when they travel to 1860 Munich on Wednesday.
